name: ElevenLabs
note: The default choice for a reason. Still unmatched for emotional range in TTS.
good: Incredible prosody, emotion control, and voice cloning accuracy. Low latency model is actually usable for real-time.
bad: Aggressive pricing that scales poorly. Hard cutoffs when you run out of credits mid-generation. API goes down more often than competitors.
price: Free tier gives 10k chars (useless). $22/mo for 100k chars. Enterprise required for real volume.

name: Deepgram
note: My go-to for STT. The speed to cost ratio is unbeatable for streaming.
good: Sub-200ms latency for streaming speech-to-text. Incredible pricing. Nova-2 model handles accents flawlessly.
bad: Their TTS offering (Aura) sounds robotic compared to ElevenLabs. STT sometimes hallucinates filler words in complete silence.
price: $0.0043/min for STT. Free tier gives $200 credit which lasts practically forever for dev.

name: Whisper (OpenAI API)
note: Great for batch transcription, terrible for real-time.
good: Zero setup, high accuracy, handles multiple languages seamlessly.
bad: High latency. No native streaming support via API. Cannot distinguish multiple speakers (no diarization).

name: Whisper.cpp (Self-hosted)
note: The only way Whisper should actually be used in production if you have compute.
good: Runs on Apple Silicon natively. Zero marginal cost. Private.
bad: You are managing infrastructure. Requires significant RAM for the large-v3 model. Cold starts are brutal if not kept in memory.
price: Free (Open source). Cost of your own compute.

name: PlayHT
note: Often considered the ElevenLabs alternative, but I find their API clunky.
good: Voice cloning is solid. Often faster generation times than ElevenLabs on standard models.
bad: Documentation is a mess. Voices often sound overly breathy. The UI is confusing and upsells constantly.

name: Speechmatics
note: The enterprise STT that nobody talks about because it isn't flashy.
good: Best-in-class accuracy for thick accents and noisy environments. Excellent real-time diarization.
bad: Enterprise sales motion. Hard to just sign up and use. Pricing is opaque until you talk to sales.

name: Rime Labs
good: Incredibly low latency. Voices are distinct and non-generic.
bad: Smaller selection of voices. Lacks the nuanced emotional control of ElevenLabs.

name: LMNT
note: Promising low-latency TTS, but struggling to stand out.
good: Very fast API response times. Clean developer experience.
bad: Voice quality can degrade into artifacts on longer generations. Support is slow to respond.
